facts.value: Receives the captured opponent as gobj and the grabbing fighter as attacker_gobj in the registered Kirby Yoshi-special callback flow. Resolves both Fighter payloads; calls ftCommon_8007DB58, ftCo_8009750C, and ftCo_800DD168 on gobj; stores attacker_gobj in x1A5C and victim_gobj; clears x221B_b5/x221B_b7; negates attacker facing into victim facing; calls ftCo_800DB368(attacker_fp,fp); requests Fighter_ChangeMotionState(gobj,0x14B,0,0.0f,1.0f,0.0f,NULL); installs ftCo_800DB464 as accessory1_cb; then calls ftCommon_8007D5D4, ftCommon_8007E2F4(fp,0x1FF), ftAnim_8006EBA4, and ftCommon_8007E2FC. No local null, kind, or distinct-object guard makes the victim specifically Kirby.
facts.rationale: Repairs reversed character attribution while preserving exact source-level operations and order.

facts.value: With a valid supplied fighter object, unconditionally sets invisible=true and calls ftColl_8007B62C(gobj,2); that callee writes x1988=2 and calls ftCo_800BFFD0(fp,2,false). Both observed Kirby-special animation callers require cmd_vars[1]!=0 and victim_gobj!=NULL, pass that victim, and clear cmd_vars[1] afterward. A null victim leaves the command uncleared by that branch. An independent subsequent cmd_vars[0]/victim guard resets the grabber's x1A6A to zero, calls ftCo_800DE2CC and ftKb_SpecialNYs_8010AC78, then clears cmd_vars[0]. Both branches can execute in one update; the second does not require the first. Independent animation-completion handling means an uncleared command is not guaranteed eventual execution.
facts.rationale: Preserves verified mutations and repairs the unsupported mandatory later-phase interpretation.
